name: What should a construction site evaluation include before buying land in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What should a construction site evaluation include before buying land in Los Angeles or the Valley?
mainEntity.text: What should a construction site evaluation include before buying land in Los Angeles or the Valley?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong pre-purchase site evaluation should go beyond a quick walk-through. It should confirm the property’s zoning, overlays, lot dimensions, easements, street access, utility connections, slope, drainage, and any obvious geotechnical or environmental concerns. In Los Angeles-area markets, this also means checking whether the site may trigger hillside rules, retaining wall needs, grading restrictions, or extra permit review. A practical evaluation should end with a buildability summary: what can likely be built, what may be difficult, what requires specialists, and what could materially increase cost or delay. Buyers should ask for a written opinion, not just verbal feedback, because that document helps compare multiple lots and avoid expensive surprises after escrow closes.
acceptedAnswer.description: A construction site evaluation before purchase should verify zoning, setbacks, access, utility availability, grading limits, drainage, soil risk, and any visible environmental red flags. It should also estimate likely permit hurdles, design constraints, and preliminary construction costs so the buyer can judge whether the site is actually buildable.
